VZ.rationale: Verizon presents a mildly attractive fundamental picture with stable, modestly growing earnings and a compelling valuation discount versus its own recent history. Q1 2026 showed solid execution: revenue +2.9% YoY, EPS +4.3% YoY, operating income expanding, and the first positive Q1 postpaid phone net additions since 2013 (55K). Management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $4.95-$4.99 (up from $4.90-$4.95), signaling confidence. The stock trades at a P/E of ~10.9x, well below the 12-month range of 10.6-21.2x and significantly below the ~17-20x levels seen through most of 2025 and early 2026. This valuation compression appears driven by the Supreme Court ruling reinforcing FCC enforcement authority (stock fell 3.8% on June 5), the Q1 revenue miss vs consensus ($34.44B vs ~$35B expected), and a -8.5% quarterly price decline. However, the fundamental trajectory is intact: broadband expansion via FWA (5.4M subscribers) and fiber (Frontier integration) provides a growth offset to mature wireless, and the company targets 750K-1M postpaid phone net additions in 2026. Risks include elevated debt (~$313B total liabilities), regulatory headwinds from the Supreme Court ruling, and competitive pressure from T-Mobile. The near-term catalyst is Q2 2026 earnings (expected soon), where investors will be watching for continued subscriber momentum, cost transformation progress, and capital allocation updates. The combination of improving fundamentals, depressed valuation vs history, and an upcoming earnings event supports a modestly positive score.
